Comments: Vestibular nucleus neurons project as mossy fibers (MF) to floccular granule cells (glutamatergic; excitatory). Transmits head angular velocity and eye velocity signals from MVN to GC. Monosynaptic; excitatory. Projection from noROI (MVN) to ROI-internal (GC).
Measurement method: Electrophysiology (extracellular and intracellular recording); anatomy (HRP retrograde labeling)

Comments: Inferior olive dorsal cap neurons project as climbing fibers (CF) to Purkinje cell dendrites (glutamatergic; monosynaptic). Transmits visual error (retinal slip) signal from IO-DC to PC as teaching signal for LTD induction. CF firing induces complex spikes; required for LTD induction during gain-up learning. Projection from noROI (IO-DC) to ROI-internal (PC).
Measurement method: Electrophysiology (extracellular recording); complex spike observation; optogenetics
Pointers on literature: Climbing fiber as error signal; Principle 1

Comments: Granule cell axons form parallel fibers (PF) in molecular layer; project to Purkinje cell dendritic spines (glutamatergic; excitatory). Transmits high-dimensional sparse context representation from GC to PC via PF. Each PC receives ~100,000 PF synapses. Site of VOR learning-related PF-PC synaptic plasticity (LTD/LTP). ROI-internal connection.
Measurement method: Electrophysiology (whole-cell patch clamp; field potential recording); synaptic plasticity experiments

Comments: Parallel fibers project to Golgi cell dendrites (glutamatergic; excitatory). GC activity excites GoC to initiate feedback inhibition circuit. ROI-internal connection.
Parallel fibers project to basket cell dendrites (glutamatergic; excitatory). GC activity excites BC to initiate feedforward lateral inhibition onto PC soma. ROI-internal connection.
Parallel fibers project to stellate cell dendrites (glutamatergic; excitatory). GC activity excites SC to initiate feedforward inhibition onto PC outer dendrites. ROI-internal connection.
A subset of mossy fibers from MVN projects directly to Golgi cells (glutamatergic). Enables feedforward inhibition of GC activity. Projection from noROI (MVN) to ROI-internal (GoC).

Golgi cell axons project (GABAergic/glycinergic; inhibitory) to granule cell dendritic claws at cerebellar glomeruli. Feedback/feedforward inhibition limits simultaneous GC firing; maintains sparse coding. ROI-internal connection.
Pointers on literature: Golgi cell inhibition of granule cells

Comments: Basket cell axons project (GABAergic; inhibitory) to PC soma and axon initial segment (pinceau structure). Powerful lateral inhibition controls PC spike generation timing and magnitude. ROI-internal connection.
Pointers on literature: Basket cell pinceau on PC axon initial segment

Comments: Stellate cell axons project (GABAergic; inhibitory) to PC outer dendritic shafts in molecular layer. Modulates CF-PF integration efficiency at climbing fiber synaptic sites on PC dendrites. ROI-internal connection.
Pointers on literature: Stellate cell synapse on PC dendrite

Comments: Purkinje cell axons project (GABAergic; inhibitory; monosynaptic) to floccular target neurons (FTN) in medial vestibular nucleus. Learned changes in PC simple-spike firing alter inhibitory drive on FTNs, thereby adapting VOR gain. Projection from ROI-internal (PC) to noROI (MVN).
Measurement method: Electrophysiology (extracellular recording); flocculus lesion; HRP anterograde labeling
Pointers on literature: Purkinje cell inhibition of FTN; neural basis of VOR learning

Comments: Vestibular nucleus FTN neurons project (glutamatergic and glycinergic) to oculomotor nucleus (CN III), trochlear nucleus (CN IV), and abducens nucleus (CN VI) via medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF). Transmits VOR eye movement commands from MVN to OMN as final motor output. noROI-to-noROI connection.
Measurement method: Electrophysiology; HRP retrograde labeling; neural tracing
Pointers on literature: VOR output pathway to extraocular muscles

Comments: Indirect inhibitory feedback pathway: PC projects (GABAergic) to inhibitory interneurons in FTN (vestibular nucleus), which in turn inhibit IO-DC. This recurrent feedback loop limits the magnitude of climbing fiber-driven early learning in cerebellar cortex (auto-regulation of learning rate). Note: indirect pathway (not monosynaptic). Projection from ROI-internal (PC) to noROI (IO-DC) via noROI interneurons.
Pointers on literature: Principle 3: recurrent feedback from PC to IO; limits early cortical learning
